rows.summary: The report gets the computed price facts largely right in the market excerpt. However, its rating reasoning rests on a fabricated $935 cost basis, unverified single-post catalysts (earnings beat, Telsey $1,135), an unsourced 90%+ renewal rate and an underived $1,000 target that contradicts its own 32-34x fair-value view. A reversed EMA direction, mislabelled TTM growth, a 22.5% vs 22.9% upside slip, post-trade-date social data and agent names in the digest compound the problems and preclude publication.

The bear-leaning conclusion is defensible, but several of its key supports are wrong: JV loss share (83%, not 74%), the bull upside (15-48%, not 30-50%), interest coverage (unsourced, and 0.25x mixes quarterly and annual periods) and debt-to-equity (4.57x, not 456x). The $10 target is not derived and contradicts the ruling's own rejection of the bear's downside. Look-ahead social data, invented baselines and fabricated quotes add to the problems, and these need correction before the note can run.

The headline computed price levels are mostly right, but the stop-distance and reward-to-risk math is wrong and the core-earnings comparison behind the ruling is methodologically flawed. The ruling leans on single-post social claims (implied move, beat streak, $58B revenue) and fabricated historical precedents, uses post-trade-date StockTwits data, and sets an underived $345 target that contradicts its own add triggers.

The underweight call rests on load-bearing misreadings. It treats a seasonal sequential decline as an 86% annual collapse when same-quarter revenue rose YoY, calls narrowing cash burn 'accelerating', and builds the technical case on a MACD divergence and volume decline that the data contradict while missing the bearish crossover that actually occurred. Add a $150 target not derived from any base case, a 19x leverage ratio that is really 0.19x, look-ahead social data, and fabricated comparables, and the report needs substantial rework before publication.

The report is well structured and its price-level facts largely match the computed data. However, the ruling and plan rest on a misread MACD 'histogram collapse', an unsourced Azure growth figure, a single-post put-sweep claim and a misread yield-curve inversion, and they also carry mislabelled fiscal quarters, several arithmetic errors including the conservative case's key math, an entry equal to the stop, and an underived $560 target. It needs substantive rework before publication.

The digest's price-derived technicals match the computed facts, and most headline ratios (growth, margins, working capital, current ratio) are recomputed correctly. However, the rating rationale rests on misread concepts: gross versus net debt, annualized OCF versus TTM FCF, debt/OCF presented as DSCR, and a mislabeled margin period. Add a TTM FCF figure that doesn't reconcile with its own quarters, inconsistent and logically unreachable exit triggers, and invented peer comparables in a bull key point, and the report is not fit to publish.

The report's core arithmetic and evidence do not hold. The price target traces to a miscomputed expected value. The trade levels ($120 entry, $105 stop) are disconnected from the $238.90 price. The ruling rests on hyperscaler capex data that appears nowhere in the inputs and on a backwards working-capital argument. Indicator reads (MACD histogram 'compression'), FCF figures, the 52-week range and leverage ratios are also misstated or inconsistent across sections, so the note needs substantial rework before publication.

The report's Hold rests on a 'compressing interest coverage' narrative and lease-spread figures that the fundamentals data either contradicts (coverage rising to 4.83x) or never contains. The price target, add/exit triggers and several headline figures (D/E, TTM OCF, 46-year streak) are wrong or underived. Price-level facts are mostly right, but misread directions, invented baselines and internal inconsistencies make it unfit to publish without substantial rework.

The report's central framing rests on misreads: the $4.53 forward estimate is treated as company guidance, and a 0.65x debt-to-equity ratio is read as 65x. The headline rally figure, the Q3-Q4 EPS math, the EPS-gap range and the margin thresholds are wrong or inconsistent across sections. The $90 target is underived and contradicts the ruling's own logic, and the add trigger and hard stop are the same event, so the note cannot be published without substantial rework.

The report's central bear argument rests on quarterly SG&A and R&D figures that do not trace to or reconcile with the fundamentals input. It misreads the MACD as lacking a bullish crossover that already occurred, and mislabels half-year figures as annualized in the bull points. A $8.50 target above the current price contradicts the Underweight rating, the exit-trigger stop attribution and math are wrong, and the bull case relies on look-ahead order news dated after the trade date, so it is not fit to publish.

The headline price facts (SMA gaps, RSI, MACD crossover, Bollinger levels) are correctly read. Around them, the report misstates the exit-trigger distances, mislabels TWD figures as US dollars in the bull points, and builds the bear's valuation case on a misreading of forward versus trailing P/E. It also relies on a fabricated flat Oct 5 session and post-trade-date news. The $550 target is underived, the rating and action conflict, and the stop and tranche structure is self-contradictory, so it is not fit to publish without substantive rework.

Price-level facts in the digest are correct, but several load-bearing pieces are not. The bear key points rest on mislabelled and invented FCF/NI ratios, the capital-deployment argument double-counts net debt reduction, and the bull's cash-flow coverage claim does not add up. The ruling leans on unsupported oil-price and historical-multiple baselines plus single-post geopolitical claims, the $168 target is not derived from anything, and agent names, emoji and chat filler remain in the text.
